headline: France Orders Mass Evacuation of 40,000 from Cap Ferret Peninsula as Southwestern Wildfires Rage Out of Control, While US Heat Dome Pushes Heat Indices to 117°F Across Expanded Zone from Oklahoma to Montana
overview: A catastrophic wildfire emergency in southwestern France has forced the boat evacuation of more than 40,000 people from the Cap Ferret peninsula in the Gironde department, with France requesting EU assistance and President Macron responding. Simultaneously, the expanding US heat dome — already the most widespread in years — surged into new territory on July 25, with heat index values reaching 117°F in central Oklahoma and Extreme Heat Warnings now blanketing a vast corridor from Arizona and Southern California north through Montana, Wisconsin, and the Dakotas. Remnant moisture from ex-Tropical Storm Bertha continues driving major river flooding along the Nueces River system in South Texas, while a sweeping Red Flag Warning complex across the Pacific Northwest threatens rapid wildfire ignition.

events.title: France Evacuates 40,000 by Boat from Cap Ferret — Gironde Wildfire Rages Out of Control
events.location: Cap Ferret Peninsula, Gironde, Southwestern France
events.summary: French authorities ordered the total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula — a major Atlantic coast tourism hotspot — as an uncontrolled wildfire tore through the Gironde department, forcing more than 40,000 people to flee by boat to Arcachon and nearby towns. The fire, burning amid worsening drought conditions, is part of a broader wildfire emergency across France and Spain, prompting President Macron to request emergency EU aerial firefighting assistance. This event is geographically distinct from the previously reported Mediterranean coast fire and represents a new and severe outbreak on France's Atlantic coast.

events.title: US Heat Dome Surges to New Extremes — Heat Index Hits 117°F in Oklahoma, Warnings Now Span Oklahoma to Montana
events.location: Oklahoma, Montana, Wisconsin, South Dakota, Nebraska, Iowa, Kansas, USA
events.summary: The massive US heat dome significantly expanded its footprint on July 25, with NWS Norman issuing an Extreme Heat Warning for central and northern Oklahoma where heat index values reached up to 117°F — among the highest readings anywhere in the country this summer. Extreme Heat Warnings were simultaneously active across eastern Montana (highs of 98–108°F), northeastern Wyoming, Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska, Wisconsin, and South Dakota, covering a zone stretching nearly 1,500 miles from the Desert Southwest to the northern Great Plains. NWS offices from Billings to Sioux Falls warned of dangerously warm overnight lows offering little relief, sharply increasing the risk of heat-related illness and death.

events.title: Spain Wildfire Emergency Escalates — 60,000 Evacuated from Madrid and Ávila Suburbs
events.location: Madrid, Ávila, and Guadalajara Province, Spain
events.summary: The wildfire emergency in central Spain escalated sharply on July 25, with blazes near Madrid and the adjacent province of Ávila prompting the evacuation of approximately 60,000 people from towns west of the capital — a significant increase from the tens of thousands previously displaced in Guadalajara province. Displaced residents were sheltered in bullrings and community centers as firefighters continued battling what authorities described as one of Spain's largest wildfires on record. The fires are being driven by extreme heat and drought gripping the broader Mediterranean region.

events.title: Bertha's Remnants Drive Major Nueces River Flooding Across South Texas
events.location: La Salle, McMullen, Live Oak, and Dimmit Counties, South Texas, USA
events.summary: After making landfall on July 24, ex-Tropical Storm Bertha weakened into a trough, but its residual moisture and runoff are now driving a major flooding crisis along the Nueces River system in South Texas. NWS Corpus Christi issued major flooding forecasts for the Nueces River near Tilden and Three Rivers, with the river at Cotulla forecast to remain above flood stage through at least July 29. Moderate to major flooding is also occurring on the Frio River near Tilden and on the Nueces near Asherton, threatening livestock, infrastructure, and low-lying communities across multiple counties.

events.title: Pacific Northwest Sweeping Red Flag Warning — 45 mph Gusts and 11% Humidity Threaten Explosive Fire Spread
events.location: Washington, Oregon, and Northern Idaho, USA
events.summary: A large and dangerous Red Flag Warning complex was active across the Pacific Northwest on July 25, covering a broad swath of eastern Washington, central and southern Oregon, and the northern Idaho Panhandle. NWS Spokane warned of southwest winds gusting to 45 mph combined with relative humidity as low as 11% across the Okanogan Highlands and Columbia Basin — conditions primed for explosive fire behavior and rapid spread of any new ignitions. The extreme fire weather comes as dozens of fires already burn across Oregon and the region, with dry lightning also threatening new starts in Idaho.

events.title: Wildfire Smoke Air Quality Crisis — Hazardous to Unhealthy AQI Levels Across Multiple US States
events.location: Upper Midwest, Great Plains, and Eastern United States
events.summary: A broad and persistent wildfire smoke event is blanketing large portions of the United States, with AirNow.gov reporting AQI values at 'red' (unhealthy) to 'hazardous' levels across multiple states from the Great Lakes to the Eastern Seaboard. The smoke originates from a combination of Canadian wildfires and the dozens of large active fires burning across Oregon and the western US, with NASA Earth Observatory tracking a week of smoky skies across North America. Health officials are urging vulnerable populations — including the elderly, children, and those with respiratory conditions — to remain indoors and limit outdoor activity.

events.title: New Mexico Monsoon Flash Flood Threat — Ruidoso Burn Scars and Mountain Communities at Risk
events.location: South Central Mountains, Northwest Highlands, Chuska Mountains, and West Central New Mexico, USA
events.summary: NWS Albuquerque issued multiple Flood Watches across a wide swath of New Mexico on July 25, driven by the monsoon season's intensifying rainfall pattern. Of particular concern is the South Central Mountains zone, which includes the Ruidoso area burn scars where stripped hillsides dramatically amplify flash flood and debris flow hazard from even modest rainfall. Watches were also active across the Northwest Highlands, Chuska Mountains, West Central Mountains, and the Gallup/Zuni Pueblo area through Saturday evening.
